Compare taxonomic genera between two columns of species names

Source: R/compare_genus_function.R
compare_genus.Rd

This function compares the genus part of scientific species names between two columns in a data frame. It returns the original data frame with additional columns: old_genus, new_genus, and genera_match.

Usage

compare_genus(df, old_col = "old_species", new_col = "new_species")

Arguments

df

A data frame containing two columns with scientific species names (e.g., "Staphylococcus aureus").

old_col

Character string. The name of the column with the original species names. Default: "old_species".

new_col

Character string. The name of the column with the new species names. Default: "new_species".

Value

A data frame with three additional columns:

  • old_genus: the genus extracted from old_col.

  • new_genus: the genus extracted from new_col.

  • genus_match: a logical column indicating whether the genera match (TRUE) or not (FALSE).

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  old_species = c("Staphylococcus aureus", "Escherichia coli"),
  new_species = c("Staphylococcus epidermidis", "Klebsiella pneumoniae")
)
compare_genus(df)
#> Extracting genus from species names
#> Identifying mismatched genera
#> Adding classification flags
#>             old_species                new_species      old_genus
#> 1 Staphylococcus aureus Staphylococcus epidermidis Staphylococcus
#> 2      Escherichia coli      Klebsiella pneumoniae    Escherichia
#>        new_genus genus_match
#> 1 Staphylococcus        TRUE
#> 2     Klebsiella       FALSE
